sections.hypothesis: Trend-vol-target leaves only when its trend votes turn, which can take weeks. Selling after a close more than 2 ATR below the high since entry, and waiting for the votes to change, cuts sharp falls by more than it costs in dips sold and fees.
sections.rationale: Plain trend-vol-target on BTC 2020-25 passes six scorecard tests and fails luck (deflated 28%); its worst drawdown is -48%, close to the 50% limit. Its exits are slow by design, so a crash is partly held. Risk: the brake may duplicate what the trend votes already do and add fees. Written after the plain strategy's results were seen; the brake's own results are unseen.
sections.rules: Implementation trend-vol-target-brake, BTCUSDT 1d, 2020-01 to 2025-10, 330 USDT, costs from kestrel.toml, default trend settings (20/60/120 days, vol 30 days, target 50%), brake_atr 2. kestrel backtest BTCUSDT --strategy trend-vol-target-brake --research <this note> --interval 1d --start 2020-01 --end 2025-10 --cash 330. Compared with run 20261113-073755-da13da (plain trend-vol-target, same settings).
sections.falsification: Compared with the plain strategy's run on the same market, period, cash and costs. The brake is adopted only if all three hold: (1) higher Sharpe than the plain version; (2) shallower worst drawdown; (3) no scorecard test that the plain version passes is failed. Otherwise the note is rejected and the plain strategy stays as it is. Run once, at brake_atr 2. Also reported: how many times the brake tripped, and in how many of those the next entry was above the exit price (it sold a dip that recovered).
sections.parameters: Trend settings at their defaults; brake_atr 2 (ATR over 14 days, Wilder).
sections.costs: About 22-23 bps a round trip. Each trip of the brake adds a sale and usually a later purchase, so the brake must earn back its extra fees. One run, one trial.

history.reason: Failed the pre-registered adoption rule: Sharpe 0.91 against 1.21 for plain trend-vol-target on BTC 2020-25 (run 20261114-090018-e4d194 vs 20261113-073755-da13da). Drawdown slightly shallower (-45.9% vs -48.3%) but return +272% vs +639%. The brake tripped 49 times and bought back higher than it sold in 28: it duplicated the trend exit and paid for it.
